description:
Reviewer follow-up: coordination across nested dispatches is acceptable internally, but it should not require a new public NodeRouter.with_coordination/2,3 API. User requested issue creation only; no implementation, commits or pushes are authorized by this task.

Scope:
- Remove the public NodeRouter.with_coordination wrapper and migrate its callers.
- Trusted event builders pass opts: [coordination: {:connector_lifecycle, connector_id}] alongside the existing action/confidential options, using a validated canonical connector ID.
- Acquire coordination inside the outer dispatch before executing the complete Engine lifecycle handler. Retain it across cleanup, database persistence, runtime reconciliation and nested dispatches; do not lock only the individual inner calls.
- Audit enable, disable, archive, runtime startup, bootstrap/retry and direct domain entry points. Current wrapper consumers include lib/zaq/engine/connector_lifecycle.ex and lib/zaq/channels/connector_runtime.ex. Direct callers must enter through a coordinated event or an internal coordination primitive at the appropriate domain boundary; they must not become unprotected.
- Keep requester tokens and ownership context private to the router, outside events/responses/broadcasts. Preserve independent receiver holds and safe async ownership handoff.
- Keep acquisition-budget and async-handoff mechanics encapsulated in Coordination and AsyncHandoff. Preserve existing acquisition timeout behavior unless a separate contract change is explicitly agreed; the timeout is not an operation execution deadline.
- Update affected API documentation/examples and migrate tests while preserving their behavioral assertions.

Action reuse assessment:
Operation: connector lifecycle exclusion and propagation across role calls.
Evidence: lib/zaq/node_router.ex already captures coordination from event.opts in dispatch and dispatch_all; existing Coordination and AsyncHandoff modules own locking and handoff. Existing ConnectorLifecycle and ConnectorRuntime own domain operations; related prior work is zaq-e5z.6 (PR #847).
Decision: reuse/extend existing dispatch options and internal coordination mechanisms; reuse existing lifecycle domain operations and Actions. No new Action or agent tool is needed for this infrastructure API refactor.
Contract: same canonical resource key across competing operations; authorization, eligibility and actor checks remain domain-owned; acquire before runtime/database locks; preserve errors, remaining budgets, exception cleanup and caller-death protection.
Consumers: BO uses NodeRouter.dispatch with supported domain events. Explicitly audit non-BO/direct startup paths before removing the wrapper.

Acceptance and verification:
- No public NodeRouter.with_coordination API or remaining callers.
- One outer coordinated dispatch protects the entire lifecycle operation, including gaps between nested calls.
- Deterministic tests prove concurrent startup cannot enter between cleanup and persistence; startup rechecks disabled/archived state after acquiring coordination.
- Preserve nested local/remote propagation, independent resources, timeout errors, exception cleanup, receiver survival after caller death, and async handoff cancellation/ownership tests, including the real RPC scenario.
- Run focused NodeRouter coordination/contract and connector lifecycle/startup regression tests, mix q and final validation per docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Do not weaken assertions; obtain explicit approval before any change to existing test behavior.
- Read docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, applicable architecture and Engine/Channels service sections; read docs/documentation.md before documentation edits.

This issue records the agreed API direction, not approval to change timeout semantics or weaken coordination guarantees.

Implementation authorized by user message "start implemenitng zaq-nuz"; supersedes issue-creation-only scope. No commits/pushes authorized. Dependency plan: zaq-nuz.1 -> zaq-nuz.2 (DAG; implementation first, consumers/docs/validation second).
Module context: NodeRouter owns routing and scope handoff; Coordination owns process dictionary/global locks; AsyncHandoff owns acquire/ack/commit. ConnectorLifecycle owns persistence/revision/actor validation, ConnectorRuntime owns fresh startup eligibility. Domain helpers must retain internal holds for direct Action/workflow/bootstrap callers; BO gets outer coordination through event opts. NodeRouter requester context is process-local and scopes cross RPC privately. Database state remains Engine-owned; no row locks span RPC. Existing tests cover nesting, exceptions, independent resources, bounded contention, async handoff, peer RPC death and linked-device startup/cleanup races.
Refactor seam: reuse event.opts for BO and Coordination.capture/run for direct internal callers; no new production abstraction. Preserve all existing observable contracts and test assertions. New tests add dispatch-level continuity and public API surface checks. Non-goals: timeout semantics, async redesign, UX changes. No new feature E2E required. Roll back/reconsider any path losing lock coverage or requiring weakened assertions.

User rejected direct Coordination access in ConnectorRuntime: keep the domain caller on NodeRouter with dispatch options. Reopening implementation review; earlier direct-internal-primitive approach is superseded. Startup callback work must remain inside the coordinated dispatch lifetime; adding an option only to the eligibility lookup is insufficient. Auditing all affected startup entry points before revising.

User clarified: all production consumers must use NodeRouter; no direct Coordination calls in ConnectorRuntime, ConnectorLifecycle, ConnectorCommand or Engine.Api. The internal-primitive exception in the original issue is superseded. Whole-operation protection must be owned by dispatch. Startup currently has three callbacks to preserve: Bridge.start_runtime (runtime specs/options), Bridge.restart_runtime (stop/build/start), and JidoChatBridge.ensure_runtime_started (bridge ID/channel IDs plus fresh eligibility). Existing sync_provider_runtime is not an exact substitute because it restarts an enabled runtime. Awaiting choice between a typed complete startup command and a caller-local dispatch continuation before changing this callback contract. Jido.Exec supervision is a separate required propagation boundary; investigate its existing ContextPropagator extension to keep scope mechanics inside router infrastructure without changing Action timeouts.

Implementing the approved complete-command approach. ConnectorRuntime prepares typed start/restart/ensure events; ConnectorLifecycle entry points dispatch complete internal lifecycle commands with the existing conditional saved-binding scope (enable always scoped). No production domain consumer accesses Coordination. NodeRouter.ActionCoordination implements the existing Jido ContextPropagator seam; workers independently acquire holds, with strict failures and preload at application start. Existing authorization remains in Actions/API and domain enable revalidation. Reusing all existing runtime/lifecycle operations; new role actions are internal dispatch boundaries, not new agent tools. Initial corrected regression run: 130 tests and 2 properties passed. Existing startup race tests migrated mechanically to a typed test bridge command with the same signals and assertions.
User requested reverting all task changes. Restored all modified tracked files and removed the three newly created implementation/test files. Implementation is reverted; no commit or push was made.
